text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- Parliamentary hearing boards on Monday gave their support to prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek's candidates for minister of justice and minister of agriculture.
- Parliamentary boards have confirmed 12 out of 18 ministerial candidates but Drnovsek is not expected to replace any of the six nominees who failed to win backing.
- The current price for a square meter of an apartment in Ljubljana is about 2,000 German marks ($1,215), which is among the highest in Europe compared to local salaries.

- The parliamentary procedures committee said a simple majority was sufficient to elect a new government in spite of complaints from right-wing parliamentry members who argued the vote needed an absolute majority.
- Parliament has not yet passed a law according to which the state would pay compensation to some 47,000 people who suffered during the World War Two.
- Workers at electronic company Iskra Semicon started a strike on Monday demanding payment of three unpayed manthly salaries from 1996.
- A law governing safety standards at Slovenian skiing resorts dates back to 1977. Experts are pushing for a new updated law to be introduced this year.
- Although building work on a new university library was scheduled to start last year, the construction has not yet begun due to archeological findings.
- Foresters are pushing for a referendum which would limit the amount of forests, nationalised after World War Two, that would be returned to former owners of large estates.
